questions.problem: Find the curvature at an arbitrary point on the curve $r(t)={t}^{2}\,i+{t}^{2}\,j+t\,k.$
questions.worked_solution:
Let $T(t)$ denote the unit tangent to the given curve as a function of the parameter $t.$ Since we are given the curve $r(t)$ parametrized by the parameter $t$ (not the arc length $s$), we will use the following formula for the curvature: 

$$
κ(t)=\frac{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$ and find its magnitude:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)k \\  & =2t\,i+2t\,j+1\,k \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{(2t)^{2}+(2t)^{2}+{1}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{8{t}^{2}+1}\end{aligned}
$$

   

Hence, the corresponding unit tangent vector is

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{8{t}^{2}+1}}(2t\,i+2t\,j+k).\end{aligned}
$$

 

Next, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t)$ and find its magnitude:

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{2t}{\sqrt{8{t}^{2}+1}})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{2t}{\sqrt{8{t}^{2}+1}})\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{\sqrt{8{t}^{2}+1}})\,k \\  & =\frac{1}{{(8{t}^{2}+1)}^{3/2}}(2\,i+2\,j-8t\,k) \\ ‖{T}^{′}(t)‖ & =\frac{\sqrt{{2}^{2}+{2}^{2}+(-8t)^{2}}}{{(8{t}^{2}+1)}^{3/2}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{8+{8}^{2}{t}^{2}}}{{(8{t}^{2}+1)}^{3/2}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{8(1+8{t}^{2})}}{{(8{t}^{2}+1)}^{3/2}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{8}\sqrt{8{t}^{2}+1}}{{(8{t}^{2}+1)}^{3/2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(t) & =\frac{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}=\frac{(\frac{\sqrt{8}\sqrt{8{t}^{2}+1}}{{(8{t}^{2}+1)}^{3/2}})}{\sqrt{8{t}^{2}+1}}=\frac{\sqrt{8}}{{(8{t}^{2}+1)}^{3/2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Find the curvature at an arbitrary point on the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by its arc length $s$, where

$$
r(s)=⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡s,\,\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡s,\,\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡s⟩,\,0\le s<2\pi .
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Let $T(s)$ denote the unit tangent to the given curve as a function of the arc length $s.$ Since we are given the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by the arc length $s$, we will use the following formula for the curvature:

$$
κ(s)=‖{T}^{′}(s)‖=‖{r}^{″}(s)‖
$$

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(s)$ and ${r}^{″}(s)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(s) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{cos}⁡s),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡s),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡s)⟩ \\  & =⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡s,\,\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡s,\,\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡s⟩ \\ {r}^{″}(s) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡s),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡s),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡s)⟩ \\  & =⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡s,\,-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡s,\,-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡s⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the curvature is  

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(s) & =‖{r}^{″}(s)‖ \\  & =\sqrt{{(-\operatorname{cos}⁡s)}^{2}+{(-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡s)}^{2}+{(-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡s)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{cos}^{2}⁡s+\frac{1}{2}{sin}^{2}⁡s+\frac{1}{2}{sin}^{2}⁡s} \\  & =\sqrt{{cos}^{2}⁡s+{sin}^{2}⁡s} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Find the curvature at an arbitrary point on the curve $r(t)$ given that its derivative ${r}^{′}(t)$ and the derivative of the corresponding unit tangent ${T}^{′}(t)$ are as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t)=⟨-4\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t),\,-4\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)⟩,\,{T}^{′}(t)=⟨-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t),\,2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)⟩\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Since we are given both the derivative of the curve ${r}^{′}(t)$ and the derivative of the unit tangent ${T}^{′}(t)$, we will use the following formula for the curvature:

$$
κ(t)=\frac{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

Now, we find the magnitudes of ${T}^{′}(t)$ and ${r}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{T}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t))}^{2}+{(2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t))}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4{cos}^{2}⁡(2t)+4{sin}^{2}⁡(2t)} \\  & =\sqrt{4({cos}^{2}⁡(2t)+{sin}^{2}⁡(2t))} \\  & =\sqrt{4} \\  & =2 \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{(-4\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t))^{2}+(-4\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t))^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{16{sin}^{2}⁡(2t)+16{cos}^{2}⁡(2t)} \\  & =\sqrt{16({sin}^{2}⁡(2t)+{cos}^{2}⁡(2t))} \\  & =\sqrt{16} \\  & =4\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(t) & =\frac{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}=\frac{\,2\,}{4}=\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
